page: Microsoft Azure B4ms is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the BS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 4 physical cores mapped to 4 vCPUs, providing a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and includes 33 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the B4ms is designed for burstable workloads rather than sustained high-compute tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25% category, as do the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, memory performance is more balanced; the passmark memory score and the small-block cached read-only memory bandwidth of 359.39 GB/sec rank in the middle 50%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also achieve average tier results, processing 5.88 million operations per second.

The burstable CPU allocation model offers a cost-effective solution for workloads with variable CPU utilization, allowing the server to accumulate credits during low-usage periods. Large-block memory bandwidth and complex tasks like medium-sized LLM inference show weak to poor performance, highlighting the server's limitations for sustained data-intensive processing. This profile makes the B4ms suitable for development environments, low-traffic web servers, small databases, and lightweight background tasks that do not require continuous maximum CPU throughput.
